title: SR-1.27 Done comes only from a passing verify
request: Closes G92 (issue #242) and the PROTECTED part of issue #243: contractList sets a signed contract's state to done whenever a file named contracts/closed/<id>.json exists (src/engine/contracts.mjs:262-265), and nothing checks what the file holds or who wrote it. PROTECTED covers only contracts/signed/ and contracts/keys/ (src/engine/vault.mjs:27), verify writes contracts/closed/ through the caller's own identity (contracts.mjs:248), and contracts/receipts/ is unprotected. So any token with write scope over contracts/**, including the token a paired device gets (src/engine/devices.mjs:85) and a cloud connector's (src/server/oauth.mjs:17), takes a contract out of the Stop-hook gate and the pre-push gate with no contract.verified record, and can rewrite its receipts. Found by the SR-0.03 red-team round and reproduced on 31 October 2026 on the main source. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: QL-1.02. It is urgent: until it lands, a stopgap fix ahead of it needs the owner's approval. On a case-insensitive file system (macOS APFS, Windows) a case variant such as contracts/Signed/<id>.json also reaches a signed contract, because PROTECTED compares exact spelling. Sensitive path (contracts and tokens): the QL-1.03 checklist applies before merge. Also closes issue #247: contractCheckSignature joined an unchecked keyid into the key path (src/engine/contracts.mjs:203), so a forged signature verified with a key planted under contracts/drafts/.

tasks.title: Verify output is immutable to every caller
requirements: contracts/closed/ and contracts/receipts/ join PROTECTED; write, append and delete under either path are refused as immutable for every token, local or remote, owner included
verify writes the closed record and appends the receipt as internal writes, so its own output still lands

PROTECTED is matched on the folded path, Unicode NFC then toUpperCase() then toLowerCase(), so a case or long-s variant such as contracts/Signed/ or contracts/ſigned/ is refused like the exact spelling on every file system (issue #243: on a case-insensitive volume the variant reaches the protected file)
the refusal reaches MCP and HTTP callers as a 4xx naming the path as immutable, never a 500, and nothing is appended to the log by a refused call

PROTECTED is checked on the resolved target as well as the requested path: the folded path, relative to the vault root, of fs.realpathSync.native of the target when it exists, or else of its deepest existing folder followed by the remaining segments, so an 8.3 short name (CONTRA~1), a case variant in any segment, a directory symlink, a junction and a file symlink inside the vault all count as the protected path; a target that is a symbolic link whose destination cannot be resolved is refused for write, append and delete; the vault root itself is resolved with fs.realpathSync.native when the vault opens, so a vault opened through a link to its folder checks paths the same way
write, append and delete check PROTECTED before anything else, including the syncFromDisk that append runs first, so a refused call never logs

syncFromDisk and recover() never record a disk change or a deletion under contracts/receipts/ or contracts/closed/ as a new version or a delete: a file there with history in this vault's log that has changed or is missing on disk is restored from the log and the drift is reported; a file with no history (a clone, a restore, a pull from another computer) is left on disk unrecorded, since a close counts only through its signature and a receipt is informational

a refused write, append or delete under a protected path answers HTTP 409 with error immutable and the path in error_description, and MCP returns isError with text starting 'immutable:' and naming the path

write, append and delete are refused as immutable on any path whose file has more than one hard link (a link count above one), because another name of the same file may be protected; this holds for every note, not only under contracts/

the vault's pre-commit hook also refuses a commit that deletes or renames a file under contracts/closed/ or contracts/receipts/ (git diff --cached --diff-filter=DR); a change there stays allowed, because verify rewrites the close record and appends to the receipt

the first internal write or append to a path under contracts/receipts/ or contracts/closed/ with no history in this log is recorded as a whole-file version of the bytes it leaves on disk, never as a splice, so materialize matches the file

verify's internal writes land for every identity that may verify, the CLI client token, a device token and a remote read token included: the internal flag skips the path-scope check, and no admin or local condition is added to it

each red-green criterion of this task that runs test/contracts-closed-protected.test.mjs has its own subtest whose name starts with <task>-cNN: (NN is the criterion's position in this task, so T1-c01: for the first), and the criterion runs only that subtest

tasks.title: State comes from the verify record, not a file
requirements: a signed contract is done when the log holds a contract.verified record for its id with ok true and the signed hash, or when contracts/closed/<id>.json is a close record whose envelope has the close payloadType and verifies under a key in contracts/keys/, and whose verified payload holds exactly the keys id, hash, ok and verified_at, with id equal to the contract's id, ok true and hash equal to the signed hash; the fields are read from the verified payload, never from keys stored beside the envelope; a computer that can write the backup can add a key under contracts/keys/ and is trusted for closes, while no token can write there; any other file under contracts/closed/ plays no part in contractList, contractGate or the pre-push gate

done is a fact about a past verify: a later failing verify of a done contract is recorded and reported but does not reopen it, because a scope criterion can fail later for changes made after the work landed
memev doctor lists every contract whose contracts/closed/<id>.json exists but which is not done under requirement 1, as a contract to verify again; nothing is rewritten or deleted
a vault written by the code at the base, whose contracts were closed by a real passing verify, reads them as done after the change

contractCheckSignature refuses any keyid that is not the 16-hex form keyId() produces, before the keyid touches a path, and accepts a signature only by the key whose keyid the contract.signed log record holds (or, with no such record, the keyid in <id>.sig.json, still 16-hex)

contract.verified records the canonical hash of contracts/signed/<id>.json as read and signature-checked by that verify, never a hash copied from the contract.signed record, and the keyid its signature verified under; the signed hash of a contract is the hash in this log's contract.signed record for its id or, with no such record (a clone, or a contract signed on another computer), the canonical hash of contracts/signed/<id>.json whose signature verifies under requirement 5; a verify counts toward done only when its hash equals the signed hash; a contract.verified record written before this change carries no hash and counts while the contract's signed files still verify under the keyid of its contract.signed record

verify writes contracts/closed/<id>.json as a close record: a DSSE envelope with its own payloadType, distinct from the contract signature's, over exactly {id, hash, ok: true, verified_at} with hash the signed hash, made with this computer's contract key, whose public file verify writes under contracts/keys/ when it is missing, so an honest close travels with the backup and verifies on every computer
the set of contracts with a counting pass survives a restart and an upgrade: it is rebuilt from the log on open or saved in graph.json with the snapshot's seq, never held only in memory
contractList and contractGate answer from that in-memory set, kept current by each contract.verified record, never from a log scan per call
with the daemon up, memev doctor relays the unverified-close check (the allow-list in doctor.mjs), and the check carries no fix: doctor --fix leaves the file and the log untouched

memev_contract_status with no arguments and the session-start card list a done contract whose latest verify failed as done, with the failing tasks of that verify, never as active work: the card says neither 'Active contract' nor 'Build these' for it, and such contracts do not count toward the card's limit of open contracts; memev gate verifies only contracts that are not done, so a done contract never blocks a push and gate appends no verify record for it

a supersedes link takes the superseded contract out of the open state, contractGate and the default status list only when the superseding contract was signed with local origin (decided by the transport, never by an argument), either in the superseded contract's session or by a caller with the admin scope, and has a counting pass of its own; until then the superseded contract stays open, in contractGate and in the default status list

contractSign validates a draft as contractDraft does, at least one task and no top-level key that contractDraft does not write, and refuses an id that already has a contract.signed record in this log, even when its signed files are gone from disk

verifier.cmd: f=$(mktemp) && node --test --test-reporter=tap test/contracts-done-from-log.test.mjs >"$f"; rc=$?; [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && grep -Eq '^# skipped 0$' "$f" && grep -Eq '^# todo 0$' "$f" && awk -v pat='^T2-c01:|^T2-c02:|^T2-c08:|^T2-c09:|^T2-c10:|^T2-c11:|^T2-c12:|^T2-c13:|^T2-c14:|^T2-c15:|^T2-c16:|^T2-c17:|^T2-c18:|^T2-c20:' 'BEGIN { n = split(pat, alt, "|") } function flush(  i) { if (cand != "") for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (cand ~ alt[i]) hit[i] = 1; cand = "" } /^[[:space:]]*(not )?ok [0-9]+ - / { flush(); name = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]*(not )?ok [0-9]+ - /, "", name); if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*ok / && name !~ /# (SKIP|TODO)/ && name !~ /\.test\.m?js$/) cand = name; next } /^[[:space:]]*type: .suite./ { cand = "" } END { flush(); for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (!hit[i]) exit 1; exit 0 }' "$f"

criteria.statement: Changes stay in scope

stop_rules: If any criterion fails after the fix: STOP, report the measured result, the failing check and file:line. Do not start the next task.
If the work needs a path outside scope: STOP and ask the owner to amend the contract. Never widen scope silently.
